name: Chinese Dynasties
description: China dynasty by dynasty, from the Shang kings to the last emperor and the republic.

checkpoints.name: Shang and Zhou
checkpoints.note: The Shang dynasty carved characters on oracle bones, and the Zhou dynasty that followed gave China the idea of a mandate from Heaven. Confucius taught about duty and the Tao Te Ching spoke of the way. In the Warring States period armies grew, and Sun Tzu wrote on war.

checkpoints.name: Qin and Han
checkpoints.note: Qin Shi Huang unified China, with a terracotta army at his tomb and walls that became the Great Wall. The Han dynasty followed, opened the Silk Road and saw the invention of paper, and in its last years the Battle of Red Cliffs in 208 split the land.

checkpoints.name: Three Kingdoms to Tang
checkpoints.note: After the Han came the Three Kingdoms, later told in a famous novel. The Tang dynasty brought poets such as Li Bai and Du Fu and the empress Wu Zetian, and the An Lushan Rebellion of 755 shook it.

checkpoints.name: Song and Yuan
checkpoints.note: Song China had movable type, the compass, gunpowder and a new Confucian thought. Mongol conquest swept away the Song and brought the Yuan dynasty of Kublai Khan, who made Beijing his capital.

checkpoints.name: Ming
checkpoints.note: The Ming rebuilt the Great Wall and the Forbidden City in Beijing, sent Zheng He's fleets across the Indian Ocean, and enjoyed novels like Journey to the West.

checkpoints.name: Qing and the republic
checkpoints.note: Manchu emperors such as Kangxi made the Qing dynasty strong, and Dream of the Red Chamber was written in this age. The Opium War and the Taiping and Boxer risings weakened it, Sun Yat-sen led the 1911 revolution that ended the empire, and civil war followed.
